title: Anchorless confidence prober for FP8/INT8 deployments
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background: As we expand FP8 and INT8 quantized model rollouts, teams need lightweight continuous validation that flags quality regressions without requiring a gold-reference for every task. Existing pipelines rely heavily on task-specific reference corpora and heavy MMLU-style runs, which are costly to run frequently in staging or can be unavailable for proprietary customer tasks.

This ticket proposes an "anchorless" confidence prober: a suite of runtime-friendly, reference-agnostic scorers that combine model-internal confidence signals, distributional drift detectors, and small task-specific probes (where available) to generate a composite quality signal for quantized profile rollouts. The goal is to detect meaningful quality drops early and trigger gating/rollback policies before customer impact.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A reproducible scoring pipeline that runs in CI and in runtime canary jobs and produces a single composite score per model/profile variant.
2) Signal sources include: predictive entropy/perplexity, response-embedding drift vs. FP32 baseline, and a small set of probe tasks (when available).
3) The composite score has tunable thresholds to map to: OK, WARN, FAIL and integrates with rollout pipelines to block canary->prod at FAIL.
4) End-to-end tests demonstrating detection of a synthetic degradation (e.g., injected quantization noise) within 3 canary passes.
5) Dashboard tile in Console showing composite score trend, top contributing signals, and recent probe failures.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: lightweight scorer microservice that pulls model outputs from canary runs and from scheduled calibration validations. Components:
- Entropy/Perplexity module (token-level and sequence-level) with robust smoothing for short responses.
- Embedding drift: cosine distance between responses from quantized profile and FP32 baseline computed over a rolling window.
- Probe harness: small, task-focused prompt sets (10-50 examples) for common tasks (QA, summarization, classification). Probes are optional; scorer must work without them.
- Aggregator: normalized z-score per signal then weighted sum -> composite. Weights are policy-driven with defaults derived from historical sensitivity analysis.
Data/storage: short-lived time-series storage (7d retention) for fast detection; links to longer-term S3 bucket for audits.
Operational: expose REST endpoint and publish metrics to Prometheus and Console.
tests_and_validation:
Unit tests for signal computation, integration tests against small quantized models (INT8/FP8 variants), and a synthetic regression test: apply targeted quantization perturbation to a validation model and assert composite score moves from OK->FAIL.
Define a canary job that runs nightly on a subset of models and asserts no FAIL-level signals.
Include randomized fuzz tests for probe harness to ensure scorer is robust to different prompt lengths and tokenization noise.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging only): run scorer on experimental INT8/FP8 profiles for two weeks; gather thresholds. Phase 2 (canary): enable scorer for canary rollouts with WARN alerts to SRE/ML Ops. Phase 3 (gate): integrate FAIL outcome as a hard gate in rollout automation; require manual override with audit log.
Backout: automatic rollback to previous profile when FAIL persists across 2 consecutive canary runs.
progress_updates:
2025-02-12: Kickoff and design review with ML Metrics and Runtime teams.
2025-02-15: Prototype entropy/perplexity module implemented; initial unit tests passing.
2025-02-18: Embedding drift prototype integrated against lightweight FP32 baseline; observed clear signal for synthetic perturbation.
2025-02-20: Aggregator weights experiment started using historical eval traces; working on Prometheus metrics plumbing and Console tile mockups.
review_feedback:
- PM (Aisha Patel): emphasize customer-facing dashboard and provide a path for teams to opt-in custom probes.
- Research (Dr. Han): suggested adding calibration-aware confidence (adjusted for temperature scaling) to reduce false positives on low-entropy but wrong answers.
- Runtime (Jamal Nguyen): requested strict CPU/memory budget for scorer to avoid impacting inference nodes; recommended deploying as a separate microservice behind rate limits.
risks:
- False positives from drift signals on benign distribution shifts leading to unnecessary rollbacks.
- Probe coverage mismatch: customer tasks may not map well to available probes.
- Cost of running probes at scale if probe sets are large.
- Embedding drift may be sensitive to prompt prefix changes; requires robust normalization.
open_questions:
1) What default weight schedule should we expose for the aggregator and should teams be allowed to override per-customer?
2) How many probe examples strike the right balance (10, 25, 50)?
3) Do we store raw responses for audit or only aggregates to reduce PII risk?
4) Should we support a reference-mode (when customers provide a gold set) that replaces anchorless signals with stronger reference-based metrics?
